description: We're tackling the Health Monitoring challenge — building software that tracks astronaut vitals in real time, detects anomalies, and predicts health risks during missions. Looking for teammates skilled in Python, ML, full-stack dev, or data visualization. Join AstroSapien and help keep astronauts safe beyond Earth!
summary: Red Frontier is an educational Mars outpost-building and survival game developed with React, TypeScript, and Three.js. Players choose a deployment, design a habitat within its crew, payload, and budget constraints, then test the outpost in a mission-specific simulation. Dust, equipment failures, and limited life-support resources force players to balance power, food, water, oxygen, and radiation protection. Clear mission objectives, unlockable deployments, saved blueprints, and post-mission recommendations encourage players to learn from each run. NASA-linked field notes connect gameplay systems to real Mars science while explaining that in-game values are simplified for learning. The project makes the challenges of living on Mars interactive and approachable, helping players understand how engineering decisions affect crew safety and mission resilience.
details:
Mars: The Last Frontier is a browser-based Mars outpost planning and survival game. Players choose from five missions, place 12 habitat and support modules on a 3D Mars base, and try to meet a mission’s crew, payload, and budget requirements. A 30-sol simulation tracks power, batteries, water, oxygen, food, temperature, dust, equipment, radiation, and crew wellness. Dust events and equipment failures create decisions, and a debrief helps players understand the outcome and improve their design.

NASA-linked field notes connect game systems to space exploration topics, including Mars conditions, power, water recovery, radiation, plants, and communications. The project aims to make those systems and trade-offs easier to explore through interactive play. We considered crew capacity, limited cargo and funding, system dependencies, dust, radiation, and the need to make the experience understandable to players. Resource values and outcomes are simplified educational game rules, not engineering specifications.

The project uses React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Vite, Zustand, GSAP, Recharts, dnd-kit, and Tailwind CSS. An optional Node.js AI Engineering Mentor can use the OpenAI Responses API when configured; otherwise, it provides built-in guidance.

SI disclosure: ChatGPT/Codex assisted with code and written content; the team reviewed and integrated the work. No AI-generated images, video, or audio were used. The demo video was captured from the game.
